podcast.body: This 1967 instrumental was the basis for a lawsuit against Led Zeppelin, alleging that "Stairway to Heaven" was lifted from it. Despite sonic similarities when played side-by-side, the legal case was won by Led Zeppelin due to "very, very stark and pronounced" differences when the songs were compared "note by note" on sheet music. "This is how Led Zeppelin beat the charges that stairway to heaven was lifted from a 1967 instrumental by a band called Spirit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This instrumental, often played by Spirit during their 1968 tour opening for Led Zeppelin, featured a guitar arpeggio. For years, Randy California and later his estate claimed that Jimmy Page ripped off this arpeggio for Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven," leading to a highly contentious court case that reached the Supreme Court in 2020 before being dismissed. "During that tour, Spirit often played an instrumental called Taras, which featured a guitar figure known as an arpeggio, which is when you play a chord by plucking its individual notes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
